task.name: postgres

task.piece: The PostgreSQL SchemaForge bundles: a workflow that builds PostgreSQL and pgvector from the sources postgres/manifest.toml pins, for every platform SchemaForge ships on, as one relocatable archive each, and publishes them with their checksums as a release of the repository; and the fetch tool, tools/postgres, that every release, developer and test uses to get the programs for its platform, refusing an archive whose checksum is not the manifest's. Nothing else: no store (t06), no change to the manifest's sources, and no release published by this task (the operator dispatches the first, after the merge).
task.before: Merged on main: MySQL's tables (t04) and everything before them; postgres/manifest.toml with its sources pinned and its assets empty, as the design session wrote it.
task.after: The operator dispatches the workflow on main; it publishes the release the manifest names; a design session writes each archive's url and sha256 into the manifest's assets from the release's SHA256SUMS. The store (t06) starts every cluster from the programs the fetch tool gives, and the spec check's Docker image is replaced by them in that task.

file.quote: one fetch tool, used by the release, by developers and by tests, refuses anything whose hash differs
pgvector is compiled into the project's PostgreSQL 18 build from the first release
a build refuses a checkout of any other

file.what: the sources (PostgreSQL's tarball and its sha256, pgvector's tag and commit), the release tag, and the assets once written
how the project's workflows are written: the runners and the checkout

reads.crates: For tools/postgres: toml for the manifest, sha2 for SHA-256, ureq (rustls, no native TLS) for HTTPS, flate2 and tar for the archive, and the standard library for the rest. No other dependency.

command.form: cargo run -q -p schema-forge-postgres -- fetch [--target <target>] prints the folder holding the programs for the target (the running platform's by default), fetching and checking them first when the cache lacks them; cargo run -q -p schema-forge-postgres -- targets prints the targets, one per line. The workflow runs on GitHub.
command.runs: The tool locally, writing only under its cache folder; the workflow on GitHub's runners.

module.step: The targets SchemaForge ships on, each built on a GitHub-hosted runner of its own: aarch64-apple-darwin (macos-15), x86_64-apple-darwin (macos-15-intel), x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (ubuntu-24.04), aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu (ubuntu-24.04-arm) and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (windows-2025). The workflow runs on a pull request that changes postgres/** or the workflow, building every target and keeping each archive as an artifact of the run, and on workflow_dispatch on main, which also publishes (step 4).

For each target: download the PostgreSQL tarball the manifest names and refuse it unless its SHA-256 is the manifest's; clone pgvector at the manifest's tag and refuse it unless HEAD is the manifest's commit. Build PostgreSQL with meson, the same options on every target: prefix a relocatable folder, -Dicu=disabled -Dssl=none -Dreadline=disabled -Dnls=disabled -Dzlib=enabled, buildtype release; install. Build and install pgvector against that installation (make with PG_CONFIG on macOS and Linux, nmake /F Makefile.win on Windows). Each failing command fails the job.

Each target's archive is postgresql-<version>-pgvector-<version>-<target>.tar.gz, holding one folder of that name with bin/ (initdb, postgres, pg_ctl, pg_dump, pg_restore, pg_isready and psql, with .exe on Windows), lib/ and share/ as installed, pgvector among them, and nothing else; before it is packed, the job proves the folder relocatable and whole: copied to a new path, initdb makes a cluster there, postgres starts it listening only on a Unix socket in a temporary folder (TCP on 127.0.0.1 on Windows), `CREATE EXTENSION vector` and `SELECT uuidv7()` succeed through psql, and pg_ctl stops it.

On workflow_dispatch on main, a last job, after every target's, publishes the release the manifest's [release] tag names (gh release create), its notes the manifest's sources, its assets every target's archive and SHA256SUMS, one line `<sha256> <archive name>` per archive; a release of that tag that exists already fails the job, so a published archive is never replaced.

build.module: The crate schema-forge-postgres, its [package.metadata.schema-forge] role = "tool", version, edition, publish, license and repository from the workspace; its dependencies the reads' crates, each at an exact version; a library and the binary of the command.

module.public: pub struct Manifest (read from postgres/manifest.toml); pub fn targets() -> &'static [&'static str]; pub fn this_target() -> Option<&'static str>; pub fn fetch(manifest: &Manifest, target: &str, cache: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, String>; pub fn cache_folder() -> PathBuf; nothing else
module.step: Manifest reads postgres/manifest.toml: the two sources, the release tag and every asset (a table of [assets.<target>] with url and sha256). A target not among targets() is `postgres/manifest.toml: <target> is not a target SchemaForge ships on`; a sha256 that is not 64 lowercase hex digits is `postgres/manifest.toml: <target>: sha256 is not one`.

fetch gives <cache>/<version folder>/<target>, the folder holding bin/, lib/ and share/: when it is there with a file .verified holding the asset's sha256, at once; else it downloads the asset's url (https only, or file: for the tests), refuses it unless its SHA-256 is the manifest's (`<target>: the archive's checksum is <sha256>, not the manifest's`), unpacks it into a temporary folder beside the cache's, refuses an entry outside the archive's one folder (`<target>: the archive holds <path>, outside its folder`), renames the folder into place and writes .verified. A target with no asset in the manifest is `<target>: the manifest has no programs for it yet`. cache_folder() is $SCHEMA_FORGE_CACHE when set, else the platform's cache folder (~/Library/Caches on macOS, $XDG_CACHE_HOME or ~/.cache on Linux, %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows) followed by schema-forge/postgres.

build.module: The command: fetch prints the folder fetch gives, or the error and exit 1; targets prints targets().

tests.how: Rust tests on archives and manifests each test makes in a temporary folder of its own, reached by file: urls; no test reaches the network. The workflow's items are proved by its run on the PR (the gate Workflow), not by Rust tests: their test is the job of the run that carries the step.
tests.prove: a manifest's target not shipped, and a checksum that is not one, are each the error naming the target
an archive whose checksum is the manifest's is unpacked into the cache and marked verified, and a second fetch reads nothing
an archive whose checksum differs is refused and leaves nothing in the cache
an archive with an entry outside its folder is refused naming the entry
a target the manifest has no programs for is the error saying so

task.agent-decides: The jobs' and steps' names and their order within the steps above, the caching of the build between runs, how each runner gets meson, ninja and its compiler; the names and the decomposition of private code in tools/postgres; the exact versions of its crates (each the newest release at least two weeks old); the granularity of the commits. Nothing else: no target, runner, source, build option, program, archive name, error text or public item other than these; no release published.

gates.note: Every gate runs from the repository root. The workflow's run is the one on the PR's head commit.

gate.expect: every test passes, one per item, none ignored

gate.cmd: gh run list --workflow postgres.yml --commit <the PR's head> --json conclusion,databaseId
gate.expect: the run's conclusion is success, with one job per target of step 1, each a success, and an artifact per target named as step 3 names its archive

gate.proves: the repository passes, the new tool among it
gate.expect: the last line is `== All checks passed`

task.forbid: postgres/manifest.toml; .github/workflows/ci.yml; .github/workflows/pages.yml; schema/**; engines/**; features/**; crates/**; specs/**; tools/specs/**; tools/architecture/**; tools/check.sh; docs/**; site/**.
task.done: The workflow and the fetch tool on the branch; every gate green and in the PR; nothing outside owns touched. After this task, every platform SchemaForge ships on has PostgreSQL 18 with pgvector built from pinned sources by the project's own CI, proved relocatable and working, and one tool gets it, checked, for a release, a developer or a test.
